title: "VERVE module 02: size factors and composition marker scores"

  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true

    dev: svg
params:
  out_dir: "/Volumes/Informatics/AlisePonsero/Krishani_CompassMe/VERVE_test"
  sample_sheet: "/Volumes/Informatics/AlisePonsero/Krishani_CompassMe/samples.tsv"
  markers_file: "/Volumes/Informatics/AlisePonsero/Krishani_CompassMe/marker_selection/markers.tsv"
  size_factor_scope: "site"     # "site" or "all"; see the note below
  size_factor_type: "ratio"     # "ratio" (DESeq2 default) or "poscounts"
  min_count: 1                  # gene kept if total count across samples is above this
  exclude_blanks: true
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      dev = "svg")
# Bioconductor packages first, tidyverse last: S4Vectors (loaded by DESeq2)
# exports rename(), first() and others that would otherwise mask dplyr
library(DESeq2)
library(GSVA)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```

# Inputs

```{r read_inputs}
out_step <- file.path(params$out_dir, "01_host")
out_dir_02 <- file.path(params$out_dir, "02_expression")
if (!dir.exists(out_dir_02)) {
  dir.create(out_dir_02, recursive = TRUE)
}

samples_meta <- read_tsv(params$sample_sheet, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(any_of(c("sample_id", "body_site", "group", "batch")))

# Case and stray whitespace in body_site would split one site into several
# groups, and a group of one sample always gets a size factor of exactly 1.
if ("body_site" %in% names(samples_meta)) {
  samples_meta <- samples_meta |>
    mutate(body_site = str_to_lower(str_trim(body_site)))
}

counts_wide <- read_tsv(file.path(out_step, "counts", "gene_counts.txt"),
                        comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(Geneid, ends_with(".bam")) |>
  rename_with(~ basename(.x) |> str_remove("\\.markdup\\.bam$"),
              ends_with(".bam"))

markers <- read_tsv(params$markers_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Samples used for normalisation and scoring
samples_used <- samples_meta
if (isTRUE(params$exclude_blanks) && "group" %in% names(samples_meta)) {
  samples_used <- samples_used |>
    filter(is.na(group) | !str_starts(group, "blank"))
}
samples_used <- samples_used |>
  filter(sample_id %in% names(counts_wide))

count_matrix <- counts_wide |>
  select(Geneid, all_of(samples_used$sample_id)) |>
  column_to_rownames("Geneid") |>
  as.matrix()

count_matrix <- count_matrix[rowSums(count_matrix) > params$min_count, ]

tibble(
  item = c("Samples in sheet", "Samples used", "Genes in matrix",
           "Genes kept", "Markers (epithelial)", "Markers (immune)"),
  value = c(nrow(samples_meta), ncol(count_matrix), nrow(counts_wide),
            nrow(count_matrix),
            sum(markers$axis == "epithelial"),
            sum(markers$axis == "immune"))
) |>
  kable()
```

# Size factors

DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, computed from cellular gene counts.
These are what module 03 uses to normalise ERV counts: ERV counts must never be
normalised by ERV counts, because a global induction would then be divided away.

**Scope.** With `size_factor_scope = "site"` the factors are estimated within
each body site separately, which is the default here. The median-of-ratios
estimator assumes most genes are unchanged between the samples it compares.
Across the three sites that assumption does not hold: the sites differ in
epithelial type, bacterial load and recoverable human transcriptome, so a
pooled estimate would absorb site differences into the factors themselves.
Estimating within a site keeps the assumption plausible and matches the
per-site analysis plan. Setting the parameter to `"all"` pools every sample,
which is only appropriate if you intend to compare across sites.

**Estimator.** `"ratio"` is the DESeq2 default and uses genes with no zero
count in any sample of the group. `"poscounts"` uses only the positive counts
per gene, which tolerates sparse matrices but changes what the factor is
estimated from; it is offered as a fallback for a site where the zero-free gene
set is too small, and any use of it should be reported.

```{r size_factors}
estimate_factors <- function(matrix_subset) {
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = matrix_subset,
    colData   = data.frame(sample_id = colnames(matrix_subset)),
    design    = ~ 1
  )
  dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = params$size_factor_type)
  tibble(sample_id = colnames(matrix_subset),
         size_factor = sizeFactors(dds),
         n_genes_used = nrow(matrix_subset))
}

if (params$size_factor_scope == "site" && "body_site" %in% names(samples_used)) {
  size_factors <- samples_used |>
    group_split(body_site) |>
    map_dfr(function(site_samples) {
      site_matrix <- count_matrix[, site_samples$sample_id, drop = FALSE]
      site_matrix <- site_matrix[rowSums(site_matrix) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
      estimate_factors(site_matrix) |>
        mutate(scope = unique(site_samples$body_site))
    })
} else {
  size_factors <- estimate_factors(count_matrix) |>
    mutate(scope = "all")
}

size_factors <- size_factors |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(library_size = colSums(count_matrix)[sample_id],
         method = str_c(params$size_factor_type, ", scope: ",
                        params$size_factor_scope))

small_groups <- size_factors |>
  count(scope) |>
  filter(n < 2)

if (nrow(small_groups) > 0) {
  cat("WARNING: these groups hold fewer than two samples, so their size factor",
      "is 1 by construction and carries no information:",
      str_c(small_groups$scope, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

size_factors |>
  select(sample_id, any_of(c("body_site", "group")), scope,
         size_factor, library_size, n_genes_used) |>
  mutate(size_factor = round(size_factor, 3)) |>
  kable()
```

A size factor should track library size. Strong departures from the diagonal
mean the factor is being driven by composition rather than depth, which is
worth knowing before it is applied to ERV counts.

```{r size_factor_plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(size_factors,
       aes(x = library_size / 1e6, y = size_factor,
           colour = if ("body_site" %in% names(size_factors)) body_site else NULL)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sample_id), hjust = -0.15, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Assigned fragments (millions)", y = "Size factor", colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Composition marker scores

ssGSEA on the two marker sets, one score per sample per axis, as raw
enrichment scores (`normalize = FALSE`). ssGSEA ranks genes within a sample, so
the scores are invariant to the size factors above; the normalisation of the
counts only makes the input comparable in scale.

**These are relative scores, not cell type proportions.** They can be compared
between cases and controls within a site, never across sites. If an ERV signal
tracks these scores, that flags composition as a confounder; it does not
quantify it.

```{r scores}
normalised <- count_matrix %*% diag(1 / size_factors$size_factor[
  match(colnames(count_matrix), size_factors$sample_id)])
colnames(normalised) <- colnames(count_matrix)
log_expression <- log2(normalised + 1)

marker_sets <- markers |>
  filter(ensembl_gene_id %in% rownames(log_expression)) |>
  split(~ axis) |>
  map(~ pull(.x, ensembl_gene_id))

present <- markers |>
  group_by(axis) |>
  summarise(
    in_panel  = n(),
    in_matrix = sum(ensembl_gene_id %in% rownames(log_expression)),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )
kable(present, caption = "Marker genes present in the count matrix")

# normalize = FALSE: raw enrichment scores. With the default (TRUE), every
# score is rescaled by the range of scores across all samples in the matrix,
# so a sample's value depends on which other samples were run with it, and
# adding cohort samples later would shift the pilot values. Raw scores are
# stable across runs, which matters for a score read only within a site.
# GSVA changed to a parameter-object interface in version 1.50.
if (packageVersion("GSVA") >= "1.50.0") {
  ssgsea_result <- gsva(ssgseaParam(log_expression, marker_sets,
                                    normalize = FALSE))
} else {
  ssgsea_result <- gsva(log_expression, marker_sets, method = "ssgsea",
                        ssgsea.norm = FALSE)
}

# Built directly from the ssGSEA matrix (gene sets in rows, samples in columns)
scores <- tibble(
  sample_id        = colnames(ssgsea_result),
  epithelial_score = ssgsea_result["epithelial", ],
  immune_score     = ssgsea_result["immune", ]
) |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

scores |>
  select(sample_id, any_of(c("body_site", "group")),
         epithelial_score, immune_score) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_score"), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  kable()
```

```{r score_plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(scores,
       aes(x = epithelial_score, y = immune_score,
           colour = if ("body_site" %in% names(scores)) body_site else NULL)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sample_id), hjust = -0.15, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Epithelial score", y = "Immune score", colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Outputs written

```{r write_outputs}
size_factor_file <- file.path(out_dir_02, "size_factors.tsv")
scores_file      <- file.path(out_dir_02, "marker_scores.tsv")
panel_file       <- file.path(out_dir_02, "markers_used.tsv")

write_tsv(size_factors, size_factor_file)
write_tsv(scores, scores_file)
write_tsv(
  markers |>
    mutate(in_matrix = ensembl_gene_id %in% rownames(log_expression)),
  panel_file
)

tibble(file = c(size_factor_file, scores_file, panel_file)) |>
  kable()
```

# Notes for the report

- Size factors come from cellular genes, never from ERV counts. Module 03
  consumes `size_factors.tsv` as it stands here.
- Size factors were estimated with scope `r params$size_factor_scope` and
  estimator `r params$size_factor_type`. A change to either is a statistical
  choice and belongs in the methods.
- Blank controls are excluded from normalisation and scoring by default: their
  gene counts are too sparse to contribute a meaningful factor, and including
  them would distort the median-of-ratios estimate for their site.
- ssGSEA was run with `normalize = FALSE`, so scores are raw enrichment
  scores and do not depend on which other samples were in the run. They are
  therefore comparable between this pilot and later cohort runs, which the
  default range-scaled scores would not be.
- The marker scores are relative, within-site only, and derived from
  CellMarker 2.0 (doi:10.1093/nar/gkac947). The exact panel used, including
  which genes were found in the count matrix, is written to
  `markers_used.tsv`.
- The epithelial axis of the current panel is weighted toward cilia and
  squamous programmes rather than generic epithelial identity, so part of what
  it measures is which epithelium is present rather than how much. This
  strengthens the case for reading the score only within a site.
